recipes.name: Round Steak Sauerbraten
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds top round steak, trimmed and sliced thin
1 (.75 ounce) packet dry brown gravy mix

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the sliced meat and brown well. Remove meat. Add the gravy mix and water and bring to a boil, stirring constantly.

Stir in the onion powder, brown sugar, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, ginger, bay leaf and salt, and ground black pepper to taste. Return the meat to the pan, reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for one hour, or until meat is tender. Remove bay leaf.
Note: You could also transfer to a casserole dish and bake covered at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 1 1/2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Round Steak Sauerbraten
raw_recipe.description: This is a simplified version of sauerbraten that does not require marinating. Sliced top round steak is browned and simmered with vinegar, brown-gravy mix, and spices. Sour cream could be added at the end of cooking.

review.reviewBody: Delicious and easy to prepare. My wife and dinner guests raved about how good this dish was, and my wife made em promise to prepare it more often. I felt the original recipe was a bit on the bland side, so I suggest using 3 tablespoons of brown sugar, 4 to 6 tablespoons of red wine vinegar (depending on taste), 2 tablepsoons of Worcesteshire, and 2 bay leaves. The results are wonderful. Make sure to serve the meat au jaus, as the broth is where most of the flavor resides.

A very tasty meal! I made it in my crockpot by putting the meat in and topping it with the remaining mixed ingredients. It turned out very tender and flavorful. As others suggested, I did up the Worcestershire, vinegar, and salt a touch for my taste. I also didn’t have a brown gravy packet so I used some beef broth base and cornstarch. Delish!

I made this today and it came out excellent! I was nervous at first because this cut of meat does run tough. I also used a saucer as opposed to a crockpot. How ever, I did make a few changes. I used a low sodium packet the dry beef gravy (0.87oz).... 1/2 teaspoon of fresh minced ginger and 1/4 teaspoon of ground black pepper. I also had to simmer for two hours to get the meat tender- stirring occasionally. 
I do recommend doubling up on the sauce mixture because as the meat is cooking, it does dry out. 
I paired this with multigrain egg noodles, sprinkled the top with grated Parmesan and it came out great! Full of flavor and very tender! Highly recommended!

My whole family loved this. I doubled the recipe but tripled the sauce and thickened it a little bit when it was finished cooking. I don't like bay leaves so I left it out. I just browned the meat then set it aside, made the sauce then added the meat back in and stuck it in the oven for 90 minutes. I made homemade noodles to go with it. This is a definite keeper for us.
Huge hit! I used beef broth instead of just water, added some cloves and garlic too. Cooked it in the slow cooker for 8 hours on high and added noodles the last 30 minutes. Delicious.

An easy to put together main dish. I subbed diced onion for the onion powder and made my own gravy, preferring that over a mix. Even with those changes, preparation was fast. The meat turned out fall apart tender and was delicious over buttered noodles. I also think this would make a wonderful open-faced sandwich served over toasted sourdough bread.

I only had beef tips, 2 lbs. I doubled the sauce as we like gravy. Although the beef was tender, I had to greatly add more ginger, granulated onion, black pepper and vinegar--a lot of vinegar, finally switching to apple cider vinegar. I used a cornstarch slurry to obtain a gravy consistency. My rating is based on the taste before all the doctoring.
This was good as is But with recommendations from others I doubled the seasoning and marinated the meat over night … will make this again
came out perfect. used the tweaks others used to be safe. 3 tbs brown sugar. 4 tbs red wine vinegar, and 2 tbs worceshire, 2 bay leafs. family loved it. will make again.

We love this recipe! All the flavors of sauerbraten without planning a week in advance! The only variations I ever make are to use apple cider vinegar in stead of red wine vinegar, since I always have that on hand, and instead of water I use beef stock for a flavor boost. If I have them on hand, I’ll toss in a handful of Golden raisins. But it’s yummy as written.

This was a delicious, quick sauerbraten. I carmelized fresh onions before I browned the meat. I also used 2 gravy packets. Added carrots to the meat just for ease of preparation. Served over red potato mashed potatoes. Because the gravy was a little thick on the meat, I used some of the potato water to thin it down. Delish! House smelled divine!
Wonderful flavor! Add a little extra brown sugar, extra splash of Worcestershire sauce and vinegar.... Bam!

Made this tonight as instructed, then put it in the slow cooker for 8 hours, the meat came out so delicious and so so tender, I wish I had made twice as much. Ate it with rice. Gonna be a go-to anytime Top Round goes on sale now!

Very flavorful sauce. I used beff base and fresh onions and garlic. I simmered covered on the stove for 30 minutes and the meat was fall apart tender. As for those who said meat was dry, mine was as well. I used top round, sliced 1/8" or so. The piece of meat was extreamly lean, very little marbeling and that why it was dry. Fat equals moisture. The leaner the meat, the dryer it will feel, or taste in your mouth.
Easy dinner. I saw this recipe and went for it last minute. I agree that vinegar and spices should have been doubled to give it a stronger flavor. I’ll do that next time for a 5-star dinner.
It was enough for me for weekend but I have 3 others to share with sad 😔 lol

In a house with 4 teenage boys who are carnivores, meat is a must on a daily! I adjusted to recipe to 8 persons. It was an absolute hit. Next time the meal will be full blown German with Purple cabbage and Spätzle. That gravy though....WOW, Even caught the wife wiping the pan with a chunk of bread, even after she said she was full. This recipe is a keeper. Thanks for sharing it.
Easy to do and good, but not as good as "real sauerbraten" that is marinated for 48 hours
so easy to put together. I throw it in the oven for 90 min and it makes a tough piece of meat fall-a-part good! even my picky kids love it. we hardly have any leftovers!

Delicious ! Only change was to use red wind instead of red wine vinegar. Used slow cooker. My go to from now on. 

Thank you!
